title: A forgiven payroll loan, and federal emergency money through the City in the same years
question: Which City-paid organizations had a federal payroll loan forgiven while their own audits show federal emergency money reaching them through the City?
finding: 8 organizations: $13.3 million of payroll loans forgiven, and $44.6 million of federal emergency money through the City in audit years 2020 to 2022. The largest: Episcopal Community Svcs of SF Inc ($3.4 million forgiven; 2021: Disaster Grants - Public Assistance $22.7 million; 2022: Disaster Grants - Public Assistance $10.4 million); Eviction Defense Collaborative Inc ($507,537 forgiven; 2022: Emergency Rental Assistance Program $5.4 million); Meals On Wheels ($1.4 million forgiven; 2021: Disaster Grants - Public Assistance $2.5 million; 2021: Special Programs for the Aging Title III, Part B $414,104; 2020: Special Programs for the Aging Title III, Part B $34,486).
how: Payroll loans: the exact-name matches in the federal loan file already used by the payroll-loan case. Emergency money: award lines in the organization’s own single audits for fiscal years ending 2020 to 2022 that carry a pandemic label or belong to the disaster-relief, relief-fund, rent-relief or recovery-fund programmes, with the City named as the pass-through body. Joined on the employer number.
limits: Two federal sources in the same years are not the same cost paid twice. The emergency programmes named in the audits (disaster relief, rent relief, meals) paid for added work, and a payroll loan could have covered staff the City did not pay for. Whether any one salary was charged to both can be answered only from the loan forgiveness application and the invoices to the City for the loan’s covered weeks. Audits name the programme, not the people. For the fiscal years covered here, the federal audit threshold depends on the start of the entity’s fiscal year. It was $750,000 in federal awards expended across all programs for years starting before October 1, 2024, and $1 million for years starting on or after that date. An entity reaches the threshold at either amount. City payments alone cannot establish how much federal funding the recipient expended.
